For years, the Iban people living in Borneo were considered one of the most terrifying communities in the world.Its members carried out ritual hunts for people.They believed that a warrior who shed blood gained strength and glory.Nowadays, this tradition is no longer cultivated, but its traces still remain in Iban homes.They never got rid of the trophies they won years ago.Martyna Wojciechowska talks to a descendant of bounty hunters.He also takes part in the skull taming ritual.

programme.title: Woman at the end of the world
programme.desc: Martyna Wojciechowska has been wandering the world for many years and looking for interesting people who share their unique stories with her.The traveler not only talks about their everyday lives, but also raises important social issues.In the tenth season of the program he will visit, among others:Spitsbergen - the largest island of the Svalbard archipelago, where it is night for a quarter of the year.He will also reach out to the Wodaabe community living in Chad, and in El Salvador he will tackle the difficult issue of restrictive anti-abortion regulations. Martyna Wojciechowska talks to Morena Herrera, who fights for women's rights in El Salvador.The country ranks first in terms of the number of murders of women.About 500 such cases are reported annually, with a population of less than 3 million.More than half of the victims of violence do not seek help and do not reveal the truth even to their closest family members.Moreover, El Salvador has one of the most restrictive anti-abortion laws in the world.Termination of pregnancy is always illegal.If a woman loses a child in unclear circumstances, she immediately becomes a suspect.The penalty for her ranges from 2 to 8 years, and if found guilty, she may be imprisoned for 50 years.A doctor can be sentenced to 6 to 12 years for performing an abortion.Anyone who knew about the situation but did not inform the authorities is also complicit.

programme.title: Taste the world with Pascal
programme.desc: Master chef Pascal Brodnicki shows viewers how to replace traditional dishes with Asian dishes.It proves that preparing an original dinner is simple and does not have to cost much.In search of culinary inspiration, he goes to Vietnam, Laos and Thailand.He shops at local markets, prepares and sells snacks on the street, and works on a rice plantation.To prove himself, he prepares exotic dishes for his Asian hosts.He tries grilled gecko and baked ant larvae, and accepts an invitation to an unusual hunt The next stop on Pascal Brodnicki's culinary journey is Laos, whose cuisine is famous for its unusual ingredients.Flowers, insects, frogs, tadpoles, insect cocoons, lizards, geckos and even squirrel meat are eaten here.Fried seaweed, khai pene, is the culinary trademark of Luang Prabang, a city located in the north of the country.In Laos, hundreds of families earn their living by harvesting seaweed.The traveling chef found out what their job is all about.For several hours he collected algae from the bottom of the Mekong, then cut them and rolled them into long sheets.
